correctness.rationale: For positive weighted graph-ball averages, coordinate maxima commute with the weighted sum of squares. Nonnegative selector matrices attain their Hilbert spectral norms on nonnegative vectors, so the nonlinear norm is a finite selector maximum. Averaging a positive top generalized eigenvector over leaf permutations inside selector groups yields the exact 4x4 compression. Both h-limits are limits of finitely many explicit matrices; first-order eigenvalue perturbation has unique coefficient sqrt(q) at the global-hub / all-self-leaf selector and proves eventual exactness. For q=2 the packaged checker gives exact rational Sylvester positive-definiteness for all other radius words at h=1/10,1,100, exact Rayleigh witnesses and characteristic-polynomial identities. Numerical tests supplement the proof and are not taken as infinite certificates.

originality.rationale: The 2014 finite-graph norm foundation and the two 2020 papers establishing counting-measure star norms and extremizers do not include a variable atomic hub mass. Exact inspection of their finite-graph, star-norm and extremizer sections identifies counting measure as a needed hypothesis. Previously available weighted variation and weighted clique-maximal claims do not imply the strong weighted-star Hilbert norm, its general finite compression, the small-hub asymmetric extremizer, or its eventual sharp high-hub formula. Published-record semantic searches surfaced no equivalent or stronger result. Remaining risk is unindexed literature or a differently phrased weighted finite-atomic maximal theorem; independent verification has not occurred.
residual_risks: Unindexed or differently formulated variable-atom star maximal-norm results may precede this theorem; mathematical originality remains a qualified self-review.
Related published results on finite stars with counting measure do not resolve variable hub mass; the precise boundary with any private or inaccessible weighted literature needs independent review.
The main proof establishes only eventual high-hub dominance, not the exact smallest dominance threshold.

value.rationale: The strong weighted Hilbert maximal norm is a natural sharp invariant of nonuniform atomic metric measure spaces. Counted-leaf symmetry need not force symmetric extremizers after hub mass changes: an exact rational certificate identifies a genuinely asymmetric branch at mass 1/10, the known symmetric benchmark at mass 1, and an opposite symmetric branch at mass 100. The two-parameter family is classified by a quadratic-size spectral formula instead of exponential radius enumeration; the eventual large-hub selector and its sqrt(q/h) sharp law add meaningful infinite-family structure. No paper-wide or external validation claim is made.
